$schema: Every fixture tools/mock_rea.py can serve that the contract table does not vouch for, and why. tools/check_mock_contract.py re-derives every entry each run: an entry that stops reproducing FAILS the build (ledger-stale). It is evidence, not a suppression list.
authority: The handler body AS WRITTEN at the pinned commit, same as src/data/CONTRACTS.json. A recorded fixture is evidence and never authority: when the two disagree the handler decides which is stale, and the fixture is never edited to agree.

sections.nonJson: Fixtures that are not JSON at all. Recorded, kept, and served as what they are.
sections.unadopted: Routes the mock has a recording for that the client does not address, so the contract table has no row (its rowRule admits consumed / declared / recorded only). Each one is still checked against its handler at the pin and carries the same columns a table row does, so the GATE agent can merge it verbatim if the client later adopts the route.
sections.findings: Fixtures the handler at the pin REFUTES. `disposition: refuse` takes the frame out of the mock's reply path (410 with the evidence); `disposition: serve` keeps it and says why the violation cannot mislead a screen.
sections.resolved: PROVENANCE, NOT AN EXEMPTION — the checker does not read this section and nothing is suppressed by it. A fixture that was REPLACED, with the command that reproduces the replacement byte for byte. Nothing here was edited: each entry names a committed blob that is a truer recording of the route than the bytes copied, so the ledger keeps the record of why tools/FIXTURES.sha256 moved.
sections.upgraded: PROVENANCE, NOT AN EXEMPTION — the checker does not read this section and nothing is suppressed by it. A route whose recording is INCOMPLETE against the handler at the pin, and which the mock therefore serves through the handler's own pure transform rather than verbatim. The bytes on disk are untouched and tools/FIXTURES.sha256 does not move: this is the same standing rule the `authority` line above states, applied where the disagreement is an ABSENCE rather than a contradiction. Every entry names the handler code that is being applied and the exact expression, so a reader can check the instrument against the server.

nonJson.evidence: `app.get('/ws/v1/machine/snapshot', admittedWebSocketHandler(_handleSnapshot))` (de1handler.dart:190-193) — still an unconditional GET, and the wrapper only takes an admission slot before delegating: admission_control.dart:168 builds `(webSocketHandlerBuilder ?? sws.webSocketHandler)(…)` with no builder passed, and :204-206 returns that handler's response verbatim. shelf_web_socket is 3.0.0, sha256 3632775c… in pubspec.lock at this pin and the last, and its web_socket_handler.dart:41-44 -> :117-118 -> :136-148 still answers a request with no `upgrade` token 404 text/html 'Only WebSocket connections are supported.' The recorded 226 bytes ARE that page, ending `</html>\n    `. Serving it 200 application/json, as the mock did, turns a recorded truth into a manufactured one. NOTE the derivation now spans two files: the 404 comes from admission_control.dart (new at this pin, `part` at webserver_service.dart:124), not from de1handler.dart. The wrapper also gives this route one answer it never had — 429 {error:'client_admission_limit'} or 503 {error:'global_admission_limit'}, retry-after 1, above 32 concurrent or 32 accepted per second from one client, 128 globally (admission_control.dart:115-121, :216-225). That is a limit, not a shape, and no recording of it exists.

`app.get('/ws/v1/machine/shotSettings', admittedWebSocketHandler(_handleShotSettings))` (de1handler.dart:194-197) — still a GET, but the wrapper is now `admittedWebSocketHandler` (admission_control.dart:145), which takes an admission slot and delegates to the same library call `(webSocketHandlerBuilder ?? sws.webSocketHandler)` (:168), returning its response unchanged (:204-206). shelf_web_socket is pinned 3.0.0, same sha256 at both pins, and its web_socket_handler.dart:117-118 still answers a request with no upgrade headers 404 text/html 'Only WebSocket connections are supported.' — the 226 recorded bytes. Nothing in the pipeline touches a /ws path. New at this pin: over the gate's limits the reply is 429/503 JSON instead of the page.

`app.get('/ws/v1/machine/shotState', admittedWebSocketHandler(_handleShotState))` (de1handler.dart:203-206; the line read `sws.webSocketHandler(...)` before the re-pin, and `webSocketHandler` no longer appears in this file at all). admittedWebSocketHandler (admission_control.dart:145-214) only meters the request against _webSocketAdmissionGate and then delegates to `sws.webSocketHandler` (:168, response returned at :204), so a request with no upgrade headers still gets shelf_web_socket 3.0.0's `_notFound()` — the same 404 'Only WebSocket connections are supported.' page; the recorded body IS that page. New at this pin: ≥32 /ws GETs per second from one client are rejected 429 application/json before reaching it.

`app.get('/ws/v1/machine/waterLevels', admittedWebSocketHandler(_handleWaterLevels))` (de1handler.dart:198-201); the wrapper delegates to `sws.webSocketHandler` (admission_control.dart:168 — a file new at this pin, `part` at webserver_service.dart:124) and returns its answer unchanged (:204-206), so the recorded body is the same 404 page shelf_web_socket 3.0.0 (sha256 3632775c…, unchanged across the pin move) emits from web_socket_handler.dart:136-148. Byte-identical to ws__v1__machine__snapshot.json. Same caveat as that entry: the wrapper adds a 429/503 admission answer this route never gave before (admission_control.dart:115-121, :216-225), unrecorded.

`app.get('/ws/v1/devices', admittedWebSocketHandler(_handleDevicesSocket))` (devices_handler.dart:259); the wrapper (admission_control.dart:145) delegates to the same `sws.webSocketHandler` (:168) and returns its response verbatim (:204-206), so the recorded body is the same 404 page.
`app.get('/ws/v1/display', _handleWebSocket)`; the recorded body is the same 404 page.

`app.get('/ws/v1/scale/snapshot', admittedWebSocketHandler(_handleSnapshot))` (scale_handler.dart:74); the wrapper delegates to `sws.webSocketHandler` (admission_control.dart:168, a file new at this pin) and returns its answer unchanged (:204-206), so the recorded body is the same 404 page from shelf_web_socket 3.0.0 (sha256 3632775c…, unchanged across the pin move), web_socket_handler.dart:136-148. Byte-identical to ws__v1__machine__snapshot.json. ScaleHandler._handleSnapshot is unchanged (old 75-140 == new 77-142, byte for byte). Same caveat: the wrapper adds an unrecorded 429/503 admission answer (admission_control.dart:115-121, :216-225).

`app.get('/ws/v1/update', admittedWebSocketHandler(_handleSocket))` (update_handler.dart:11); the wrapper (admission_control.dart:145) delegates to the same `sws.webSocketHandler` (:168), so the recorded body is the same 404 page. The `canCheck` refusal added to `handleCommand` is a post-upgrade message path and does not touch the plain GET. `updateHandler?.addRoutes` is conditional, as it already was at the old pin.
`app.get('/ws/v1/plugins/<id>/<endpoint>', _handlePluginSocketEndpoint)`; recorded for id=time-to-ready.reaplugin, endpoint=timeToReady. The same 404 page.

findings.evidence: the inline `app.get('/api/v1/machine/cupWarmer', …)` answers exactly `{'temperature': t.toInt(), 'enabled': await bengle.getCupWarmerEnabled(), 'currentTemperature': await bengle.getCupWarmerCurrentTemperature()}`. Three keys. The recording has no `enabled` at all and carries three `prewarm*` keys the handler never writes — pre-heat moved to its own route, GET /api/v1/machine/cupWarmer/preheat, whose CupWarmerPreheatState.toJson is {enabled, leadMinutes, active}.
findings.retires: . `prewarmEnabled|prewarmLeadMinutes` is a forbiddenSpelling in the contract table: is the previous skin's `resolvePrewarm` reading prewarm* off THIS route and concluding, permanently, that the firmware had no pre-warm. `gate-d` scans the client for that spelling. Nothing scanned the frames the client is developed against — and this is one of them.
findings.why: The fixture predates the pre-heat split. It is a recording of an older ReaPrime, not of the server at the pin.
findings.bench: re-record GET /api/v1/machine/cupWarmer from a Bengle machine on current ReaPrime; until then the mock refuses the route and any cup-warmer control renders its absent state. the previous skin's git HEAD carries the same stale bytes (md5 4881ad9e…, identical to the working-tree copy), so a re-copy does NOT fix this one.

resolved.evidence: The bytes copied were the previous skin's UNCOMMITTED working-tree edit: 221203 B, md5 ab6b9472…, byte-identical to api__v1__shots__cd020a51-….json, i.e. the by-id response pasted over this route's file — 426 measurements on a route whose handler is `jsonOk(shot?.toJsonWithoutMeasurements())`. The committed blob at 5705362 is 1984 B with keys [annotations, id, stopReason, timestamp, workflow] and no `measurements` key: a recording of THIS route, of the shot d5139a1f that was latest when it was taken. Swapping in the committed blob is not editing a fixture — it replaces a paste with a recording, which is what the contract check asks for.
resolved.consequence: getShotsLatest went from 410-with-evidence (and a `no-fixture` coverage note reading 'only a REFUTED recording') to a served 200. tools/FIXTURES.sha256 moved for this file: 1c03ea7c… → the hash of the committed blob.

resolved.evidence: The copied bytes had 21 items for limit=20, with one shot cd020a51 PREPENDED to a recorded 12–13 Aug page — a frame `shot_dao.getShotsPaginated`'s SQL LIMIT cannot produce. The committed blob at 5705362 has items=20, limit=20, offset=0, total=321: the page as recorded. Same uncommitted the previous skin working-tree edit as the latest-shot one, same swap.
resolved.consequence: The `invariant` finding stops reproducing, so the ledger entry that declared it had to go with it (an entry that no longer reproduces is `ledger-stale`, by design). tools/FIXTURES.sha256 moved for this file: 7b9c9f9d… → the hash of the committed blob.

resolved.evidence: RE-RECORDED FROM THE RUNNING MACHINE, read-only: GET http://192.0.2.10:8080/api/v1/machine/ledStrip -> 200 The old bytes are a real recording and were never edited; what changed is that they disagree with the machine about the 16-bit spelling. Recorded: frontStrip/backStrip/frontSwitch all sleeping 4A4A2B2B0000, awake FFFFC1C18080 -- every channel BYTE-REPLICATED. Machine, now: sleeping 400022000000; awake FF00D900A000 (front strip and front switch) and FF00D3008E00 (back strip) -- every channel SHIFTED INTO THE HIGH BYTE, and the two strips no longer identical. The awake values match the end-to-end run. earlier run/the end-to-end notes section 3.5 exactly, which read FF00D900A000 and FF00D3008E00 off the tablet before writing anything, so this is the same machine state an earlier run measured and not a one-off. Same byte length as the file it replaces, no trailing newline either side.
resolved.consequence: The fixture now agrees with the machine that audit F-044 already made the skin agree with. F-044 (FIXLOG S-6, 29 Aug) changed led8to16 from replication to a high-byte shift on the strength of the machine over this recording -- ': the machine is the truth teller' -- and deliberately did NOT edit the fixture, because a recording is evidence. replaces the recording with a newer recording, which is a different act from editing one. led-colour.js's decode path takes the high byte and ignores the low one, so both spellings still decode identically and nothing that reads this fixture changes meaning; test/settings-bespoke.test.mjs asserts exactly that (ledColour16ToHex8('FFFFC1C18080') === ledColour16ToHex8('FF00C1008000')). tools/FIXTURES.sha256 moved for this file: 3900117e827ed6e04e146b65279e69ead85408252a24aada05dbad90bf8657d9 -> 27142cbb449b9fcdcf6605bde8db7d0dceb50a4180812aa3361efecde4e377ef. mock-contract and gate-d re-run green after the swap.

upgraded.declaredBy: fix run 6 — the History power page
upgraded.handlerSymbol: MachineSnapshot.toJson (through ShotRecord.toJson / ShotSnapshot.toJson, served by ShotsHandler._getShot)
upgraded.evidence: machine.dart:64-140 — the three derived channels are 'computed on read from the raw [pressure] and [flow] fields — never stored — so already-recorded history shots gain these channels with zero migration ([fromJson] does not read them; [toJson] recomputes them)'. toJson (:176-186) writes puckResistanceDerived / loadImpedanceDerived / hydraulicPowerDerived conditionally; _derivedOrNull (:70-76) is the gate. ShotSnapshot.toJson calls machine.toJson() per measurement and ShotsHandler._getShot answers jsonOk(shot.toJson()), so a ReaPrime at the pin serves these keys on EVERY recorded shot wherever the gate passes.
upgraded.observed: The three recorded shot fixtures carry 923 measurements between them and ZERO *Derived keys (and zero `sensors` maps). They are recordings of an older ReaPrime, taken before the getters existed — an incomplete recording, not a server without the feature.
upgraded.transform: For each measurement, with p = machine.pressure and f = machine.flow: write puckResistanceDerived = p/(f*f), loadImpedanceDerived = p/f and hydraulicPowerDerived = 0.1*p*f only when f >= 0.3 and p >= 0.3 and every input and result is finite. Keys are OMITTED below the gate, never written null — key presence IS the validity signal (src/data/rea-names.js:48-53). Measured over the three fixtures: 34/50, 317/336 and 124/136 in-shot samples gain the keys.
implementedIn: tools/mock_rea.py — upgrade_recorded_shot(), applied in do_GET for /api/v1/shots/{id} only
test/fixtures/history-route-fixture.js — upgradeRecordedShot(), the same rule in the other language, for the rendering suites and the capture battery's screen states
upgraded.why: The History power page (fix run 6) is the first surface that renders the derived channels, and with the recordings as they stand every instrument would photograph its honest empty state instead of the chart. Editing the fixtures was refused: a fixture edited to pass a check has stopped being a recording, and FIXTURES.sha256 would have moved for three files with no truer recording behind the change.
upgraded.bench: Re-record GET /api/v1/shots/{id} from a machine on current ReaPrime and this entry retires: the recording will carry the keys and the transform becomes a no-op. Until then it is the instrument answering as the pinned server answers.
